title: Design a notification / push system
relevance: High — classic 45-min HLD at FAANG + Indian product cos (Meta, Uber, Flipkart, PhonePe, Amazon, Microsoft); probes async queues, multi-channel delivery (APNs/FCM/SMS/email), preferences, idempotency, and priority isolation.
company_notes: Common across campus/new-grad and experienced HLD loops; baseline expects channels + queue decoupling + preferences + retries, while experienced depth focuses on priority isolation, idempotency timing, provider limits, campaign pacing, webhook status, and burst-QPS estimation.

phases.goal: Lock scope, reliability goals, and traffic-isolation expectations before drawing components.

must_hit.point: In-scope flow includes user or segment notifications over push/email/SMS, supports immediate and scheduled sends, and returns basic delivery status.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They name channels, immediate vs scheduled, and status tracking as explicit requirements.

must_hit.point: Out-of-scope boundaries are stated: no custom APNs/FCM transport, no full template CMS/A-B UI, no ML ranking unless requested.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They proactively cut non-core product analytics/CMS/ML work to protect interview time.

must_hit.point: NFRs separate critical and bulk paths: OTP/security cannot be delayed by campaigns, and accepted requests must not be silently dropped.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They explicitly call out traffic isolation and durable acceptance semantics.

must_hit.point: Clarifications include transactional vs promotional split, channels in scope, in-app inbox need, and retention horizon.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They ask targeted scoping questions before proposing architecture.

probes: What exact requirements would you lock in the first 5 minutes, and what would you declare out of scope?

hints.1: Start by separating functional scope from non-functional guarantees.
hints.2: Force a decision on transactional vs marketing traffic and whether in-app is required.
hints.3: State durable accept + no silent drop + priority isolation as mandatory, then defer CMS/ML ranking.

phases.goal: Convert average and burst traffic into capacity targets that drive queue and worker sizing.

must_hit.point: Candidate contrasts 10M notifs/day (~115/s average) with burst shape (1M campaign in 5 min, ~3.3K/s) and designs for ~5K/s surge.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They explain peak is the governing constraint, not daily average.

must_hit.point: Channel mix assumes push highest volume, email lower, SMS lowest due to cost and provider constraints.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They reserve SMS for high-value use cases and avoid SMS-heavy defaults.

must_hit.point: Worker parallelism is derived from desired send QPS and provider RPS per connection, with pooled HTTP/2 for APNs/FCM.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They tie partition/consumer counts to provider throughput limits, not arbitrary worker counts.

probes: If average load looks easy, what burst assumption changes your design and why?

hints.1: Estimate both average and campaign spikes.
hints.2: Map burst QPS to queue partitions and independent worker pools.
hints.3: Use the 10M/day vs 1M-in-5-min contrast and design around ~5K/s surge.

phases.goal: Define asynchronous intake, status visibility, and ownership boundaries for producers, users, and providers.

must_hit.point: Primary intake is POST /v1/notifications with idempotency_key and template-driven payload, returning 202 Accepted with notification_id.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They keep intake non-blocking and avoid waiting on APNs/FCM/SMS providers.

must_hit.point: User/device surfaces include GET/PUT /v1/users/{id}/preferences and PUT /v1/devices for token registration/refresh.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They separate producer send APIs from user-owned preference/device APIs.

must_hit.point: Status retrieval and provider callbacks are explicit (GET /v1/notifications/{id}, POST /internal/provider-callbacks/{channel}).
must_hit.evidence_hint: They include asynchronous status updates from webhooks rather than only request-time state.

probes: What request/response contract would you expose so producers never block on downstream providers?

hints.1: Think intake + tracking + preferences/devices as separate API groups.
hints.2: Make send asynchronous and add status polling/callback ingestion.
hints.3: Use POST /v1/notifications -> 202, then status endpoint and internal provider callback endpoint.

phases.goal: Capture entities needed for routing, dedupe, retries, and compliance-safe preference enforcement.

must_hit.point: Model preferences per (user_id, notification_type, channel) with quiet_hours_start/end and timezone.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They enforce per-type/per-channel opt-in logic before delivery.

must_hit.point: Notification and DeliveryAttempt are separate: Notification stores intent/idempotency metadata; DeliveryAttempt stores channel target, status, provider_msg_id, attempts, and error.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They distinguish logical notification from per-channel/per-device attempts.

must_hit.point: Dedupe store uses Redis SETNX idempotency key with TTL, including example 24h transactional retention and longer campaign windows.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They place dedupe in a fast key-value store and mention bounded TTL.

must_hit.point: Device token model stores user_id, device_id, platform, token, updated_at and supports pruning invalid/unregistered tokens.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They explicitly handle multi-device fan-out and token lifecycle cleanup.

probes: Which tables/records are mandatory to avoid duplicate sends and to support multi-device delivery?

hints.1: Split user intent from channel-level attempts.
hints.2: Add preference/timezone and device-token lifecycle state.
hints.3: Include Notification + DeliveryAttempt + Preference + Device + Redis dedupe key with TTL.

phases.goal: Present a decoupled pipeline that isolates priorities and channels while remaining restart-safe.

must_hit.point: Intake path performs validation/auth/idempotency, persists (row or outbox), then publishes to Kafka/SQS rather than calling providers inline.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They guarantee durable accept before enqueue-driven processing.

must_hit.point: Traffic is split by priority and/or channel into separate topics and worker pools so promo lag cannot block OTP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They avoid shared consumer lag across critical and bulk flows.

must_hit.point: A scheduler handles schedule_at/digests and re-inserts due work into the same queueing pipeline.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They avoid one-off special paths for delayed sends.

must_hit.point: Channel workers are independently scalable (APNs/FCM, email, SMS) with retries/DLQ, while tracking/webhook updates remain off the send critical path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They isolate provider-specific failures and keep delivery state updates asynchronous.

probes: Draw the end-to-end flow from producer request to provider send and status update.

hints.1: Start with producer -> API -> queue -> workers.
hints.2: Add scheduler, preference/template/device lookup, and per-channel workers.
hints.3: Use priority-separated topics/worker pools plus webhook-based status updates.

phases.goal: Defend critical reliability and product tradeoffs under failure, scale, and compliance pressure.

must_hit.point: Delivery semantics are at-least-once with dedupe before provider call; exactly-once claims are rejected as unrealistic across providers/networks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They explain timeout-after-send duplicate risk and pre-send idempotency protection.

must_hit.point: Preference caching strategy includes fast reads plus invalidation on writes; quiet-hour bypass policy is explicit for critical security/payment cases.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They discuss correctness of preference changes, not only cache latency.

must_hit.point: Campaign fan-out is paced by generator/cursor workers and provider-aware throttling, never exploded inline in the API.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They separate campaign creation from paced message materialization.

must_hit.point: Provider outage handling uses circuit breaker and optional secondary provider, while preserving channel isolation.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They describe failover behavior without cross-channel cascading failure.

probes: How do you prevent duplicate SMS/OTP when provider timeouts make send outcome ambiguous?
How would you handle quiet hours and campaign pacing without breaking critical alerts?

hints.1: Focus on one failure mode: timeout after provider may still have accepted.
hints.2: Explain ordering of dedupe, retries, and preference checks.
hints.3: Commit to at-least-once + pre-send idempotency key, then pace campaigns and define critical bypass rules.

phases.goal: Identify primary scaling and failure choke points and give concrete mitigations.

must_hit.point: Bulk queue lag is controlled via more partitions/workers, with strict protection so bulk consumers cannot steal critical capacity.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They mention independent consumer groups or worker pools for critical vs bulk.

must_hit.point: Provider 429 and quota pressure is handled with token buckets, backoff, and campaign smoothing per provider and tenant.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They throttle proactively instead of only reacting to failures.

must_hit.point: Hot Redis preference/token paths are reduced through sharding by user_id and short-TTL local worker caches.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They reduce repeated remote reads on the routing hot path.

must_hit.point: Tracking/webhook write amplification is reduced by batching and TTL/archival, and never blocks send execution.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They keep analytics durability concerns from delaying outbound delivery.

must_hit.point: Failure safety requires durable accept before 202, restart-safe workers via idempotency, plus DLQ and replay tooling.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They can recover from crashes without silent loss or uncontrolled duplicate sends.

probes: What are your top bottlenecks at surge time, and what exact controls keep OTP healthy during a bulk campaign?

hints.1: Look at queue lag, provider limits, and hot cache keys first.
hints.2: Map each bottleneck to one concrete mitigation and isolation rule.
hints.3: Protect critical lanes, throttle bulk, shard/cache hot reads, and keep durable-accept + DLQ replay.

tradeoffs.topic: Shared queue simplicity vs priority-isolated topics/worker pools
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Choose separate priority lanes so overload stretches marketing latency but does not delay OTP/security traffic.

tradeoffs.topic: Claimed exactly-once vs at-least-once with idempotency/dedupe
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Acknowledge exactly-once is not realistic across providers; use at-least-once, dedupe keys, and idempotent business identifiers before provider calls.

tradeoffs.topic: Inline campaign fan-out vs paced generator/cursor workers
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Keep API lightweight and enqueue campaign creation, then pace fan-out to provider quotas to avoid burst collapse.

tradeoffs.topic: Single provider simplicity vs multi-provider resilience
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Single provider is simpler initially, but circuit breaker and optional secondary provider reduce blast radius for provider outages.

tradeoffs.topic: Push-only delivery vs push plus in-app path
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Use in-app/WS when users are online and APNs/FCM for offline delivery; optionally coalesce noisy social events before send.

gotchas.trap: Calling APNs/Twilio synchronously from order/payment request paths.
gotchas.correction: Return 202 after durable accept and process through async queues/workers.

gotchas.trap: Using one topic/queue for OTP and marketing traffic.
gotchas.correction: Isolate priorities with separate topics and worker pools to avoid head-of-line blocking.

gotchas.trap: Claiming exactly-once delivery without idempotency design.
gotchas.correction: State at-least-once semantics and implement dedupe/idempotency keys.

gotchas.trap: Applying dedupe only after provider success.
gotchas.correction: Set dedupe before provider call to prevent timeout-induced duplicates.

gotchas.trap: Ignoring preferences, quiet hours, or unsubscribe handling.
gotchas.correction: Gate sends through per-type/per-channel preferences with explicit bypass policy only for critical alerts.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting multi-device token handling and invalid-token cleanup.
gotchas.correction: Store per-device tokens and aggressively prune unregistered/invalid tokens.

gotchas.trap: No distinction between transient retries and permanent failures.
gotchas.correction: Use backoff+jitter for transient errors, drop/cleanup hard failures, and route unresolved cases to DLQ.

gotchas.trap: Building custom persistent phone transport instead of using APNs/FCM.
gotchas.correction: Treat Apple/Google push infrastructure as transport and focus your system on routing, reliability, and tracking.

gotchas.trap: Trying to fan out millions inline in campaign API calls.
gotchas.correction: Create campaign metadata first, then pace fan-out asynchronously with quota-aware workers.

gotchas.trap: Designing only for average QPS without surge estimation.
gotchas.correction: Use burst assumptions to size partitions, workers, and provider throttling.
